cards.title: The expiry date hides in plain sight
cards.body: Tiny print, shiny foil, half of it snipped off. Checking it properly takes ten seconds and saves a lot of doubt.

cards.title: Find "Exp", not "Mfg"
cards.body: Strips usually show both. Mfg is when it was made. Exp is the one that matters for use.

cards.title: Month and year format
cards.body: Many labels show only a month and year. If you're unsure how to read the date on your strip, ask your pharmacist.

cards.title: Don't cut through the date
cards.body: When you snip off a tablet, cut away from the printed date and name. A loose tablet with no label is a guessing game.

cards.title: Check at the counter too
cards.body: Glance at the expiry when you buy, especially for things used slowly, like SOS tablets or syrups.

cards.title: Opened bottles have their own clock
cards.body: Some drops and syrups should be used within a set time after opening. The label or leaflet says so. Write the opening date on it.

cards.title: Expired? Set it aside
cards.body: Don't use expired medicines. Ask your chemist about safe disposal, and get a fresh supply if it's still needed.

takeaway: Check the Exp date, keep it intact when cutting strips, and write opening dates on drops and syrups.
share: Send this to whoever guards the family medicine box.
